home.title: Install architectures, not dependencies.
home.lede: Source code, AI rules and MCP servers, injected into your repo and pinned to a commit. Your AI already knows how to use it.
home.installMore: Other ways to install: npm, npx, specific versions →
home.askExample: Add GitHub login to this project with genpm
home.layersText: Every package carries its code, the rules your AI needs to use it, and the MCP servers it talks to. All three pass through the same SHA check.
home.graftLabel: The three layers of a package pass through SHA verification and land in your project
home.codeText: Lands in src/, not in node_modules. You see it in your diff, edit it and commit it.
home.contextText: An AGENTS.md per module, loaded only when your agent works in that folder.
home.connectionsText: The MCP servers a module needs, declared in its manifest. Added only with your consent.
home.step1Text: Find a module by need, from the web, the CLI or your AI.
home.step2Text: Read the exact files, the AI rules and the commit before anything touches your repo.
home.step3Text: Code lands in src/, rules go where your IDE reads them, and the lockfile pins the SHA.
home.aiText: One MCP server. Your agent searches, inspects and installs, and asks you before adding anything outside your code.
home.secTitle: What you reviewed is what gets installed.
home.secShaText: Tags resolve to a 40-character commit, verified after every fetch. Never a branch.
home.secScriptsText: GenPM has no lifecycle hooks. Nothing from a package runs on your machine.
home.secScanText: Every AI rule file is checked for prompt injection before it is listed.
home.pubText: Tag a release, add a genpm.json and an AGENTS.md. The registry stores metadata only; your code stays on GitHub.
home.empty: No packages yet. Be the first to publish one.

mcp.title: Ask your AI to install it.
mcp.lede: The GenPM MCP server gives your agent the same engine as the CLI. It can search, inspect and inject modules, and it always asks before touching anything outside your code.
mcp.step1Title: Add the server to your client
mcp.step2Text: Eight tools. No publish, login or force: credentials stay outside the agent’s reach.
mcp.t_search: Find packages by need. Sponsored results are never returned to agents.
mcp.t_info: Read a package: manifest, rules, MCP and scan, before installing.
mcp.t_add: Plan and inject. Dry run first; asks you before MCP config or npm installs.
mcp.t_list: What is installed in this project, with versions, SHAs and local changes.
mcp.t_remove: Remove a package and its rules cleanly; never deletes code you modified.
mcp.t_audit: Verify integrity, signatures and security advisories.
mcp.t_validate: Validate a package you are authoring before publishing.
mcp.s1Text: A package’s MCP servers are only added after you confirm, with the full command shown.
mcp.s2Text: The server only writes inside the project root, through the same path checks as the CLI.
mcp.s3Text: npm dependencies are proposed, never installed silently.

publish.title: Publish your architecture.
publish.lede: Your code stays on GitHub. Pick a repository, we check what it needs and generate the genpm.json for you.
publish.s2Text: An AGENTS.md with Purpose, Map, Integration, Conventions and Don't.
publish.s3Text: Tags are immutable. Branches are rejected.
publish.s4Text: Verifies the tag, scans the rules, lists the package.
publish.c1: A LICENSE file that matches the license declared in genpm.json.
publish.c2: AGENTS.md under 16 KB, with the five recommended sections.
publish.c3: No secrets, no .env files, no build output in the injected tree.
publish.c5: A summary your users understand in one line.

security.title: How GenPM protects your project
security.lede: Secure by design, verifiable by anyone. We never promise 100 %: we promise invariants with tests that block every release.
security.inv1: Integrity: the installed bytes are exactly the commit’s tree.
security.inv2: Zero execution: GenPM never runs package code or hooks.
security.inv3: Confinement: writes stay inside your project, in planned paths.
security.inv4: No executables: injected files never keep execute permissions.
security.inv5: Consent: no MCP config, npm installs or overwrites without your yes.
security.inv7: Registry authority: publishing reads GitHub, never the client.
security.inv8: Signed manifests: the CLI only installs registry-signed manifests.
security.inv9: Immutability: a published version never changes.
security.inv10: Tenant isolation: no query crosses registries.
security.reportText: Email hello@genpm.net (subject [SECURITY]) or use GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting. First response within 48 hours. Safe harbor for good-faith research.

trusted.title: Trusted publishing
trusted.lede: Publish from GitHub Actions without storing any token: Actions proves which repository and workflow is running (OIDC) and GenPM gives it a 15-minute token that can only publish to this scope from that repository.
trusted.noScopes: You do not administer any scope yet. Publish your first package to claim yours.
trusted.none: No repository can publish here without a token yet.
trusted.how: Add id-token: write to the job permissions and run genpm publish: with no GENPM_TOKEN it asks Actions for an OIDC token and exchanges it automatically.
trusted.howGitlab: GitLab CI: declare id_tokens with aud genpm as GENPM_ID_TOKEN and run genpm publish. GitLab projects can only publish through trusted publishing, and must be public.
